consideredAndDeclined.item: Decision 6 says gates 2 and 3 hold 'for those eight NT classes' while NT-4 is discharged rather than named
consideredAndDeclined.observation: Gate 3 asks that each remainder be already named at a condition-4 obligation with an owner. Seven classes are named; NT-4 is not named under DR-131's label.
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: The join recorded at D-148 established that NT-4 adds no distinct execution obligation because its contract pass is 'Refused under DR-133', so there is no separate remainder for gate 3 to require a naming of — and the executions that discharge it, DR-133 NT-1, NT-2 and NT-3, are themselves named at G21 and G23 with owners. The entry does not blur this: it states the seven as named and NT-4 as discharged, in separate clauses. Pressing the entry to argue the gate-3 theory for NT-4 would push a recording act into the eligibility determination that gate 4 reserves — the same reason I withdrew a repair limb at D-145 turn 2.

independence.priorParticipation: I accepted the artifact whose fifth kind this act performs, consented to the four preceding instances of this template, and the doctrine sentence in Decision 6 exists because of a MUST-FIX I raised at D-147. Five consents in a row on one template, plus seeing my own correction quoted back, is the strongest pull toward approval by recognition in this whole sequence. So I reconstructed the after operand in code rather than reading a diff, counted the gate table again, re-derived the eight-class placement across five adopted acts, audited the D9 question on its own, and re-checked every refusal after stripping blockquote markers.

coordinatorSummary: CONSENT at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with no advisories. Fifteen attacks run, none landed. Custody is clean and the MF-6 is unapplied: 90a56a37 at 0444 unmoved, HEAD never left b077633, file 08 still at 27 gate rows with no DR-G28, and all four file pins plus the D-153 commit pin reproducing. D-153's application checks out byte-for-byte against what it consented to. On mechanics I changed method for the closing act rather than repeating a diff read: I reconstructed the after operand by applying the five intended edits to the before operand in code, and the reconstruction equals the stated block exactly, which proves no sixth change hides in it. The before operand is byte-exact and occurs exactly once in the whole file, all three fenced blocks are backslash-free with no edge whitespace, the row carries eight fields in the header's order, DR-G28 is free, the anchor is real, and Limb B names the identifier in the same act so condition 4 holds at 24 of 24 — figures that reconcile against a table I counted myself at 27 rows, 24 OPEN and 3 HARD-BLOCKED. The risk unique to this kind is D9 minting, since its whole subject is the host not minting D9 classes, so I audited it separately: every D9 token in the draft is the bare string with no coined identifier, the claim is a prohibition, the evidence column points only at the existing v1.14 mapping, and the refusal appears four times. The row also tracks the contract — its claim covers NT-7's pass and its evidence column covers NT-8's. Decision 6 is the moment this chain closes, and it is stated correctly: seven classes named across G24 through G28, NT-4 discharged on the separate basis D-148 recorded, gates 2 and 3 held to those two gates only, gate 1's application-grade limb expressly not established, and gate 4 reserving eligibility to a later dedicated cycle. It also states, unprompted, that CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and binds NOTHING are not themselves a Class A bar, citing D-085 — the doctrine correction that took a MUST-FIX to establish at D-147 turn 1, arriving here without being asked. Two items are recorded as considered and declined, including the one substantive question beyond arithmetic: whether gates 2 and 3 can be said to hold for NT-4 when it is discharged rather than named. After this act all eight DR-131 NT classes are placed, D-149's five kinds are all performed, and what remains for DR-131 is harness execution and a later SATISFIED-GRADE cycle.
